claim: AWS Control Tower sets up and governs a multi-account environment that follows prescriptive best practices, orchestrating AWS Organizations, AWS Service Catalog and IAM Identity Center to build a landing zone.
question: What is AWS Control Tower, and which services does it orchestrate?

values.display: set up and govern an AWS multi-account environment
orchestrates the capabilities of several other AWS services
to build a landing zone

evidence.quote: AWS Control Tower offers a straightforward way to set up and govern an AWS multi-account environment, following prescriptive best practices. AWS Control Tower orchestrates the capabilities of several other AWS services, including AWS Organizations, AWS Service Catalog, and AWS IAM Identity Center, to build a landing zone in less than an hour.

claim: Control Tower orchestration extends the capabilities of AWS Organizations and applies controls (guardrails) to keep organizations and accounts from drifting away from best practices.
question: How is Control Tower related to AWS Organizations?

values.display: extends the capabilities of AWS Organizations
AWS Control Tower applies controls

qualifiers.scope: AWS Control Tower and AWS Organizations

evidence.quote: AWS Control Tower orchestration extends the capabilities of AWS Organizations. To help keep your organizations and accounts from drift, which is divergence from best practices, AWS Control Tower applies controls (sometimes called guardrails).

claim: AWS says that if you host more than a handful of accounts, an orchestration layer such as Control Tower helps with account deployment and governance, and Control Tower can be the primary way to provision accounts and infrastructure.
question: When does AWS suggest using Control Tower?

values.display: more than a handful of accounts
your primary way to provision accounts and infrastructure

evidence.quote: If you are hosting more than a handful of accounts, it’s beneficial to have an orchestration layer that facilitates account deployment and account governance. You can adopt AWS Control Tower as your primary way to provision accounts and infrastructure.

claim: AWS describes Control Tower as the easiest way to set up and govern a secure, compliant, multi-account AWS environment based on best practices.
question: Which service does AWS call the easiest way to set up and govern a secure multi-account environment?

values.display: the easiest way to set up and govern
a secure, compliant, multi-account AWS environment

evidence.quote: In short, AWS Control Tower offers the easiest way to set up and govern a secure, compliant, multi-account AWS environment based on best practices established by working with thousands of enterprises.

claim: A landing zone is a well-architected multi-account environment based on security and compliance best practices; it holds all OUs, accounts, users and other resources that you want under compliance regulation.
question: What is a landing zone?

values.display: a well-architected, multi-account environment
the enterprise-wide container

evidence.quote: Landing zone – A landing zone is a well-architected, multi-account environment that's based on security and compliance best practices. It is the enterprise-wide container that holds all of your organizational units (OUs), accounts, users, and other resources that you want to be subject to compliance regulation.

claim: Account Factory is a configurable account template that standardizes provisioning of new accounts with pre-approved configurations; it can create and enroll accounts and automatically applies controls and policies to them.
question: What is Account Factory?

values.display: a configurable account template
pre-approved account configurations
automates the process of applying controls and policies

evidence.quote: Account Factory – An Account Factory is a configurable account template that helps to standardize the provisioning of new accounts with pre-approved account configurations.
The Account Factory can create and enroll AWS accounts, and it automates the process of applying controls and policies to those accounts.

claim: Account Factory works as an account vending machine built on provisioned products in AWS Service Catalog.
question: Which AWS service is Account Factory built on?

values.display: vending machine
provisioned products in AWS Service Catalog

evidence.quote: Automated account configuration: AWS Control Tower automates account deployment and enrollment by means of an Account Factory (or “vending machine”), which is built as an abstraction on top of provisioned products in AWS Service Catalog.

claim: When it sets up a landing zone, Control Tower creates the Security OU and an optional Sandbox OU, creates an IAM Identity Center directory (or lets you self-manage your identity provider), and applies all mandatory preventive and detective controls.
question: What does Control Tower create when it sets up a landing zone?

values.display: the Security OU and the optional Sandbox OU
Creates a cloud-native directory in IAM Identity Center
allows you to self-manage your identity provider

qualifiers.scope: landing zone set up through the console

evidence.quote: When you create your landing zone through the console, AWS Control Tower creates two AWS Organizations organizational units (OUs). These are the Security OU and the optional Sandbox OU, contained within the organizational root structure.

Creates a cloud-native directory in IAM Identity Center, with preconfigured groups and single sign-on access, if you choose the default AWS Control Tower configuration, or it allows you to self-manage your identity provider.
Applies all mandatory, preventive controls to enforce policies.

claim: Control Tower preventive controls are not applied to the management account; the root user and administrators in the management account can perform work that controls would otherwise deny, and their actions are still logged in the log archive account.
question: Do Control Tower controls apply to the management account?

values.display: Preventive controls are not applied to the management account
This exception is intentional
continue to be tracked in the logs

evidence.quote: Preventive controls are not applied to the management account.

The root user and any administrators in the management account can perform work that controls would otherwise deny. This exception is intentional. It prevents the management account from entering into an unusable state. All actions taken within the management account continue to be tracked in the logs contained within the log archive account, for purposes of accountability and auditing.

claim: The shared accounts of a landing zone are the management account, the log archive account and the audit account, provisioned during setup.
question: Which shared accounts does Control Tower provision?

values.display: the management account, the log archive account, and the audit account
provisioned during setup

evidence.quote: In AWS Control Tower, the shared accounts in your landing zone are provisioned during setup: the management account, the log archive account, and the audit account.

claim: The log archive account is a repository for API activity and resource configuration logs from all accounts; the audit account is a restricted account that gives security and compliance teams read and write access to all accounts.
question: What do the log archive account and the audit account do?

values.display: a repository for logs of API activities and resource configurations
a restricted account
your security and compliance teams

evidence.quote: This account works as a repository for logs of API activities and resource configurations from all accounts in the landing zone.
The audit account is a restricted account that's designed to give your security and compliance teams read and write access to all accounts in your landing zone.

claim: AWS does not recommend running production workloads from the Control Tower management account; create a separate account for workloads.
question: Should workloads run in the Control Tower management account?

values.display: It is not recommended to run any type of production workloads
Create a separate AWS Control Tower account

evidence.quote: It is not recommended to run any type of production workloads from an AWS Control Tower management account. Create a separate AWS Control Tower account to run your workloads.

claim: Control Tower sets up an organization-level CloudTrail trail with the landing zone, which logs all events for the management account and all member accounts; it relies on trusted access.
question: How does Control Tower centralize CloudTrail logging?

values.display: an organization-level trail
logs all events for the management account and all member accounts

evidence.quote: AWS Control Tower sets up a new CloudTrail trail when you set up a landing zone. It is an organization-level trail, which means that it logs all events for the management account and all member accounts in the organization.

claim: Control Tower logs actions automatically through CloudTrail and AWS Config, including actions from the management account and from member accounts.
question: Does Control Tower log actions taken in the management account?

values.display: All actions are logged
including actions from the AWS Control Tower management account

evidence.quote: All actions are logged, including actions from the AWS Control Tower management account and from your organization's member accounts.

claim: Preventive controls are implemented with SCPs, RCPs and declarative policies; detective controls with AWS Config rules; proactive controls with CloudFormation hooks.
question: Which mechanism implements each kind of Control Tower control?

values.display: Resource Control Policies (RCPs), and declarative policies
The detective controls are implemented using AWS Config rules
implemented using AWS CloudFormation hooks

evidence.quote: The preventive controls are implemented using Service Control Policies (SCPs), Resource Control Policies (RCPs), and declarative policies, which are part of AWS Organizations.
The detective controls are implemented using AWS Config rules.
The proactive controls are implemented using AWS CloudFormation hooks.

claim: Preventive controls prevent actions from occurring; detective controls detect events when they occur and log them; proactive controls check resources before they are provisioned and do not provision noncompliant resources.
question: What is the difference between preventive, detective and proactive controls?

values.display: Preventive controls prevent actions from occurring
Detective controls detect specific events when they occur
before the resources are provisioned

evidence.quote: Preventive controls prevent actions from occurring.
Detective controls detect specific events when they occur and log the action in CloudTrail.

Proactive controls check whether resources are compliant with your company policies and objectives, before the resources are provisioned in your accounts. If the resources are out of compliance, they are not provisioned.

claim: Mandatory controls are always applied and cannot be changed or deactivated because they protect Control Tower resources; elective and strongly recommended controls can be changed at any time.
question: Can mandatory controls be turned off?

values.display: Mandatory controls are always applied, and they can't be changed
they can't be deactivated
You can change the elective or strongly recommended controls

evidence.quote: You can change the elective or strongly recommended controls that are in force, at any time, from the AWS Control Tower console or the AWS Control Tower APIs. Mandatory controls are always applied, and they can't be changed.
These controls are applied to your OUs by default when you set up your landing zone, and they can't be deactivated, because they protect AWS Control Tower resources.

note: d066; landing zone 4.0 note: mandatory controls are no longer applied by default (control-behavior page), see control-tower-lz4-mandatory-not-default

claim: Control guidance has three categories: mandatory controls protect resources that Control Tower deploys, strongly recommended controls enforce common best practices, and elective controls track or lock down commonly restricted actions; the last two apply at the OU level.
question: What do mandatory, strongly recommended and elective mean for Control Tower controls?

values.display: These controls protect AWS Control Tower-deployed resources
enforce some common best practices
track or lock down actions

evidence.quote: Mandatory controls are enforced in your landing zone depending on what you may have enabled in your environment. These controls protect AWS Control Tower-deployed resources.
Strongly recommended controls are designed to enforce some common best practices for well-architected, multi-account environments. These controls apply at the OU level, for all accounts in that OU.
Elective controls enable you to track or lock down actions that are commonly restricted in an AWS enterprise environment. These controls apply at the OU level, for all accounts in that OU.

claim: Starting with landing zone version 4.0, mandatory controls are no longer applied by default.
question: Are mandatory controls applied by default in landing zone version 4.0?

values.display: Landing Zone version 4.0
mandatory controls are no longer applied by default

qualifiers.scope: Control Tower landing zone version 4.0 and later

evidence.quote: Starting with AWS Control Tower Landing Zone version 4.0, mandatory controls are no longer applied by default.

note: d078; the changes lens records the date

claim: A control applies to an entire OU, so every account in the OU is affected and users in any account of the landing zone are always subject to the controls of their account's OU.
question: At what level are Control Tower controls applied?

values.display: A control applies to an entire organizational unit (OU)
every AWS account within the OU is affected

evidence.quote: A control applies to an entire organizational unit (OU), and every AWS account within the OU is affected by the control.

claim: Control Tower now uses the term control; the earlier term guardrail means the same thing.
question: What is the difference between a guardrail and a control in Control Tower?

values.display: These terms are synonymous for our purposes
the previous term, guardrail

evidence.quote: During this time, you may see the previous term, guardrail, as well as the new term, control, in our documentation, console, blogs, and videos. These terms are synonymous for our purposes.
